html.body: Date: 2025-03-05 REMARKSClaims 1-16 are currently pending in the application. Claims 1 and 11 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over US 2020/0207336 to Cho in view of US 2020/0211071 to Rosas-Maxemin. Claim 2 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of US 2018/0292832 to Bae. Claims 3, 5, and 9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of US 2015/0254981 to Tachibana. Claim 4 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas- Maxemin in view of US 2022/0197305 to Kim. Claim 6 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Bae and Kim. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Tachibana and Kim. Claim 8 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas- Maxemin in view of Bae and Tachibana. Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Kim and Tachibana. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of US 2021/0089020 to Shimamoto. Claim 13 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Bae and Shimamoto. Claims 14 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Tachibana and Shimamoto. Claim 15 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Kim and Shimamoto. Reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the remarks and amendments submitted herewith.Amendments to the Claims Independent claims 1 and 11 have been amended.Specifically, independent claims 1 and 11 have been amended to recite that the empty parking space sensor is a pressure sensor, a radar sensor or a sonar sensor using radio waves configured to detect whether or not there is the parked vehicle in the target parking space, and a server positioned at parking place or remotely located from the parking place, the server is further configured to continuously acquire the vehicle information from the vehicle and determine a status of the vehicle, the status including a vehicle speed of the vehicle and a yaw rate of the vehicle.Support for these amendments may be found in the specification, figures and claims as originally filed. No subject matter has been disclaimed or abandoned and the amendment of certain claims is not to be construed as a dedication to the public of any of the subject matter of the claims as previously presented. No new matter has been entered through these amendments and entry is respectfully requested.Summary of Examiner Interview Jeremy Justice thanks Examiner Neleski for the telephonic interview of February 24, 2025.The specification, claims and drawings of the instant application were discussed in view of the 35 USC §103 rejections in view of Cho and Rosas-Maxemin. A tentative agreement was reached regarding the proposed amendments to the independent claims, which are formally presented herein, overcoming the U.S.C. §103 rejections. However, the Examiner indicated that an updated search and consideration would be required.Entry of this statement of substance of interview is requested as the statement is in compliance with 37 C.F.R. §1.133.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. .103 As noted hereinabove, claims 1 and 11 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho in view of Rosas-Maxemin. Claim 2 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Bae. Claims 3, 5, and 9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Tachibana.Claim 4 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Kim. Claim 6 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas- Maxemin in view of Bae and Kim. Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Tachibana and Kim. Claim 8 is rejected under 35 U.S.C.§103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Bae and Tachibana. Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Kim and Tachibana. Claim 12 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Shimamoto. Claim 13 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Bae and Shimamoto. Claims 14 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Tachibana and Shimamoto. Claim 15 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin in view of Kim and Shimamoto. The rejections are respectfully traversed.The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. KSR, 550 U.S. at 416, 82 USPQ2d at 1395; Sakraida v. AG Pro, Inc., 425 U.S. 273, 282, 189 USPQ 449, 453 (1976); Anderson 's-Black Rock, Inc. v. Pavement Salvage Co., 396 U.S. 57, 62- 63, 163 USPQ 673, 675 (1969); Great At. & P. Tea Co. v. Supermarket Equip. Corp., 340 U.S.147, 152, 87 USPQ 303, 306 (1950). Further, "a prior art reference must be considered in its entirety, i.e., as a whole, including portions that would lead away from the claimed invention." W.L. Gore & Assoc., Inc. v. Garlock, Inc., 721 F.2d 1540, 220 USPQ 303 (Fed. Cir. 1983), cert.denied, 469 U.S. 851 (1984).As tentatively agreed to during the telephone interview, the Applicant respectfully submits that neither Cho nor Rosas-Maxemin, either alone or in combination, expressly or inherently disclose, teach, and/or fairly suggest each and every feature of amended independent claims 1 and 11. Specifically, the Applicant submits that the cited art references fail to expressly or inherently disclose, teach, and/or fairly suggest the amended features of amended independent claims 1 and 11 regarding the empty parking space sensor is a pressure sensor, a radar sensor or a sonar sensor using radio waves configured to detect whether or not there is the parked vehicle in the target parking space, and a server positioned at parking place or remotely located from the parking place, the server is further configured to continuously acquire the vehicle information from the vehicle and determine a status of the vehicle, the status including a vehicle speed of the vehicle and a yaw rate of the vehicle.Further, Applicant respectfully submits that Bae, Tachibana, Kim, and Shimamoto, either alone or in combination, fail to cure the defects of Cho of Rosas-Maxemin, either alone or in combination.Based on the foregoing, the Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1 and 11, and all claims which depend thereon, are not obvious in view of Cho and Rosas-Maxemin, either alone or in combination. Therefore, the Applicant respectfully submits that independent claims 1 and 11, are patentable over Cho and Rosas-Maxemin, wither alone or in combination.The Applicant respectfully requests that the rejections be withdrawn and independent claims 1 and 11, and all claims that depend thereon, be held in a condition for allowance.Conclusion In view of the above remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the application is now in condition for allowance. The Examiner is encouraged to contact the undersigned to resolve efficiently any formal matters or to discuss any aspects of the application or of this response.Otherwise, early notification of allowable subject matter is respectfully requested.No additional fees are believed to be due. However, the Director is hereby authorized to charge all required fees (including any extension of time fees) and to credit any overpayment of fees in this and any concurrent or future correspondence to Deposit Account No. 041133.Respectfully submitted, /Jeremy J.
